articles.title: 76ers rule out LeBron James, Joel Embiid vs. Hornets
articles.summary: The Philadelphia 76ers have ruled out LeBron James and Joel Embiid for Saturday night’s road matchup against the Charlotte Hornets as the organization manage...
articles.body:
The Philadelphia 76ers have ruled out LeBron James and Joel Embiid for Saturday night's road matchup against the Charlotte Hornets as the organization manages both stars' injuries during the second half of a back-to-back.

Philadelphia's latest injury report lists James as out due to low back/sciatica management, while Embiid will sit because of right foot plantar fascia injury management.

The 76ers (5-1) enter Saturday's contest following a 98-93 victory over the New York Knicks in Friday night's NBA Cup opener, extending their strong start to the 2026-27 season.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

James and Embiid both played significant minutes in the victory despite Philadelphia missing Jaylen Brown, who was ruled out shortly before tip-off with left patellar tendinopathy.

James finished with 20 points, nine rebounds, eight assists, one steal and one block across 34 minutes. The 41-year-old shot 8-for-15 from the field and 2-for-6 from beyond the arc.

Embiid contributed 10 points, seven rebounds, seven assists, one steal and one block in 33 minutes. The 32-year-old struggled offensively, shooting 3-for-12 from the field and missing all four of his 3-point attempts.

76ers face additional injury concerns against Hornets

Through five appearances, James is averaging 16.4 points, seven rebounds, seven assists, 1.6 steals and one block while shooting 44.9% from the field.

Embiid is averaging 19.2 points, 9.4 rebounds, 5.2 assists and one block across 35.2 minutes per game, shooting 40% from the field.

Philadelphia's injury report also lists Dominick Barlow (low back stress reaction) and Ariel Hukporti (right Achilles tendon rupture) as out.

Brown remains questionable with left patellar tendinopathy, alongside Tacko Fall (left quadriceps strain) and Jabari Walker (left patellar tendinopathy).

With James and Embiid unavailable, Philadelphia could rely more heavily on Tyrese Maxey and its remaining rotation players to maintain its early-season momentum.

The 76ers will face the Hornets (3-3) Saturday at 6 p.m. ET on NBA TV.

articles.title: Analyst urges Houston to consider Kyrie Irving trade
articles.summary: After the Houston Rockets’ loss to the Dallas Mavericks in NBA Cup group play on Friday, one analyst believes the Rockets should go all in on trading for Kyr...
articles.body:
After the Houston Rockets ' loss to the Dallas Mavericks in NBA Cup group play on Friday, one analyst believes the Rockets should go all in on trading for Kyrie Irving . The Dallas Mavericks pulled off a clutch-time victory over the Rockets, winning 116-111. Irving finished with 35 points, 9 assists, and 4 rebounds, and knocked down 5 three-pointers.

Following the game on Saturday afternoon, SiriusXM NBA Radio analyst Sam Mitchell said he believes the Rockets should push the trade for Irving. Mitchell started by saying Irving has exceeded expectations in Dallas, especially given the doubts about how he would look after his injury.

"Kyrie is making everybody on that team better. Everybody thought this was going to be a down year for Dallas with a young coach straight from college, with all these young players transitioning to building this team around Cooper. Nobody knew what Kyrie was going to look like. Man, Kyrie looked better than he did before he got hurt."

He then addressed Irving's trade value , arguing a team could land him without giving up a huge haul.

"You might be able to get two first-round picks for Kyrie [unclear: "down"], and that's a lot for a 34-year-old injured point guard who missed all of last year with an injury."

Mitchell then named the Rockets as the team that should make the move, saying Houston's competition in the West makes the timing ideal.

"I'll tell you right now: the Houston Rockets. You put him on the Houston Rockets, you put him on the Houston Rockets with the injuries in the rest of the West, it might be over. They are clearly the best team with Kyrie out there."

If the Rockets were to trade for Irving, it would be a reunion for Kevin Durant, who played with Irving in Brooklyn before the championship-winning point guard was sent to the Dallas Mavericks. Durant was traded to the Phoenix Suns at the 2023 trade deadline.

articles.title: Rangers' Joc Pederson, Kyle Higashioka and Jakob Junis decline mutual options
articles.summary: ARLINGTON, Texas (AP) — Designated hitter Joc Pederson, catcher Kyle Higashioka and right-hander Jakob Junis declined their mutual options with the Texas Ran...
articles.body:
ARLINGTON, Texas (AP) — Designated hitter Joc Pederson, catcher Kyle Higashioka and right-hander Jakob Junis declined their mutual options with the Texas Rangers, the team said Saturday.

All three became eligible for free agency.

Pederson turned down an $18 million option that did not include a buyout, part of a $37 million, two-year contract . The 34-year-old, a two-time All-Star, hit .235 with 26 homers and 53 RBIs in 136 games. He did not play after Sept. 12, when he fractured his left wrist upon getting hit by a 93.3 mph fastball from Arizona's Brandon Pfaadt.

Higashioka declined a $7 million option and gets a $1 million buyout, completing a $13.5 million, two-year contract . The 36-year-old hit .218 with seven homers and 18 RBIs in 56 games this year. He played his last major league game on July 20 because of a right flexor strain , then played in 11 games at Triple-A Round Rock from Sept. 4-20 during an injury rehabilitation assignment.

Junis turned down a $5 million option and receives a $1.25 million buyout as part of a $4 million, one-year contract . The 34-year-old was 1-3 with a 3.64 ERA in 52 relief appearances. He didn't pitch between June 29 and July 18 because of hip impingement and between July 28 and Aug. 15 because of a left adductor strain.
